title: Your phone keyboard guesses your next word.
kit: Your phone keyboard guesses your next word.
Copilot does the same thing with a much bigger memory. Its guesses sound right because it learned from a huge amount of text.

title: What Copilot really does.
kit: Copilot writes by predicting the next word, one word at a time, from patterns in the text it learned from.
…it picks a likely next word. Numbers and dates are words too.
It predicts. Without the source, it guesses or searches the web, and nothing checks it against Mutla's policy.

title: It writes by guessing the next word.
kit: It writes by guessing the next word.
At each step, every possible next word gets a score. The model picks one and repeats.
It predicts likely words. Mutla's policy says 15, but 30 is more common.
Unused annual leave may be carried over up to
Percentages are illustrative. Mutla's policy says 15 days.

title: A colleague with your keycard.
kit: They can open every door you can open, and no other door. That is how Copilot reaches your work files.

title: Copilot opens only your doors.
kit: With a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, Copilot can use the files, emails and chats you already have permission to open. A restricted folder stays closed.
Your permissions decide what Copilot can see.

title: What Copilot can see.
kit: With a Microsoft 365 Copilot license (the M365 Copilot (Premium) label), Copilot uses only what you can already open. On Copilot Chat (Basic), it uses the web and the files you upload, and you also get Copilot in Outlook. M365 Copilot (Basic) adds Copilot in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Your access is the limit. The decision about what to share is still yours.

title: Some decisions stay with people.

title: Redact before you ask.
kit: To redact is to remove or replace every detail that identifies a person or is sensitive, before the text goes anywhere.
Replace names with roles. Remove numbers, salaries and medical details.

title: Four moves before any prompt.
kit: Then read it once more: could someone outside HR tell who this is?
Names become roles: Employee A, Colleague B.
ID and phone numbers are removed.
Salaries and allowances of named people are removed.
Medical and case details that point to a person are removed.

title: Data is not the same as sources.
kit: Block 3 · two inputs people mix up
Data is not the same as sources.
Data is the facts of this case: the role information, the figures. Approved sources are the rules to follow: the template, the policy.
Data says what is true here…
…sources say how it must be done.
Give both. Without rules, Copilot ignores the template. Without facts, it invents details.
